newsitem.title: USA: NY's Pataki wants Washington to stiffen gun laws.
newsitem.headline: NY's Pataki wants Washington to stiffen gun laws.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said Tuesday he would push Washington to strengthen gun control laws, saying Sunday's deadly shooting spree on the Empire State Building made the need for such laws plain.

Ali Abu Kamal, a 69-year old man who carried a Palestinian passport, bought a .038-caliber Beretta semiautomatic handgun from a gunshop in Florida and used it to shoot six tourists, killing a member of a Danish rock band, before shooting himself to death on top of the national landmark building.
"I think that the Empire State Building shows how critical it is that we have intelligent and aggressive federal policy. New York can't do it alone," Pataki told reporters in Albany.

He continued, "What we need is a clear federal commitment both in enforcement and passing laws that protect states such as New York from states such as Florida who haven't done, in my opinion, the right thing."

Pataki's comments echoed criticism voiced by New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and gun control advocates who bitterly decried the ease with which a foreign visitor to the United States could purchase a powerful gun.

Kamal arrived in the country on Dec 24, and while he bought the gun legally under Florida and federal laws, would have had to meet stricter identification and residential requirements in New York, Giuliani has noted.

Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles has defended his state against critics, saying, "It is far from true that the state is cavalier about its gun laws." Other Florida officials said that if Kamal bought the gun after being in the United States just three weeks, he either lied or the background checks failed at the federal level.

Pataki said he did not expect to call Florida's governor on Tuesday, saying his Administration was considering how best to approach Chiles. He added he was asking for action at both the federal level and the state level.
